sentences.«Hvorfor er du i Norge?» spurte UDI på d: "Why are you in Norway?" the UDI asked at the first interview.
sentences.Jeg hadde aldri en plan om å komme til m: I never had a plan to come to dark, cold Norway.
It just turned out that way.
sentences.På fabrikken skjønte jeg at jeg trives b: At the factory I realised that I am happiest working with people, not with machines.
sentences.Jeg pleier å si til ungdommene som jeg j: I usually tell the young people I work with that they have to think about these things:
sentences.Hvorfor er jeg her i Norge?: Why am I here in Norway?
sentences.Hva vil jeg fortelle familien min hvis j: What do I want to tell my family if I get to see them again?
sentences.Vil jeg fortelle dem at jeg har tatt utd: Do I want to tell them that I have got an education, a job and maybe friends here in Norway, or do I want to tell them that everything is difficult?
sentences.Derfor var jeg aktiv som frivillig i Rød: That's why I was active as a volunteer in the Red Cross Youth in Hedmark.
There I made lots of Norwegian friends.
sentences.Senere har jeg også blitt kjent med mang: Later I have also got to know lots of Norwegians through the jobs I have had.
sentences.Det er vanskelig å fortelle om vonde tan: It is difficult to talk about painful thoughts when you are not good at Norwegian.
A conversation with Abdul from Afghanistan.
sentences.Da Abdul var liten, var familien på fluk: When Abdul was little, the family was on the run all the time.
sentences.De flyttet fra by til by i Afghanistan f: They moved from town to town in Afghanistan because there was war.
sentences.Skolene var ofte stengt fordi de ble bom: The schools were often closed because they were bombed.
sentences.Derfor gikk Abdul bare fire år på skole: That's why Abdul only went to school for four years in his home country.
sentences.Da Abdul var 17 år, flyktet han alene fr: When Abdul was 17, he fled Afghanistan alone.
sentences.Etter noen måneder på flukt kom han til: After a few months on the run he came to Norway.
sentences.Nå er han 31 år og jobber som miljøveile: Now he is 31 and works as a support worker and bilingual assistant in Elverum municipality.
sentences.Hvordan var den første tiden i Norge?: What was the first period in Norway like?
sentences.Det var vanskelig å tilpasse seg den nye: It was difficult to adapt to the new culture and learn a new language.
sentences.Jeg gikk på grunnskole for voksne på Ham: I went to primary and lower secondary school for adults in Hamar, and afterwards I got a job at a factory in Kongsvinger.
sentences.Vi produserte plastikkdeler til biler de: We made plastic parts for cars there.
I worked there for two years.
sentences.Når du er ung, vet du ikke hva du vil bl: When you are young, you don't know what you want to be.
sentences.Derfor kan det være fint å prøve litt fo: That's why it can be good to try a few different things.
sentences.Har du tatt utdanning i Norge?: Have you got an education in Norway?
sentences.Ja, jeg tok studiespesialisering på vide: Yes, I took general studies at upper secondary school.
sentences.Jeg ble pappa, og jeg måtte jobbe mye ve: I became a dad, and I had to work a lot alongside school because my wife was also at school.
sentences.Senere tok jeg faget «flerkulturell fors: Later I took the subject "multicultural understanding" at Oslo and Akershus University College.
sentences.Jeg har også tatt et år sykepleierutdann: I have also done a year of nursing training.
sentences.Hva slags arbeidserfaring har du i Norge: What kind of work experience do you have in Norway?
sentences.Siden 2008 har jeg jobbet med flyktninge: Since 2008 I have worked with refugees in Norway.
sentences.Først var jeg nattevakt på et asylmottak: First I was a night watchman at an asylum reception centre, and later I got a job in a home for unaccompanied minor refugees.
sentences.Nå jobber jeg som miljøarbeider og tospr: Now I work as a support worker and bilingual assistant at the adult education centre in Elverum.
sentences.Har du blitt litt norsk?: Have you become a bit Norwegian?
sentences.Jeg har alltid tenkt at det er viktig å: I have always thought that it is important to adapt to the new society, but I have never thought about becoming Norwegian.
sentences.Jeg vil være afghaner sammen med mine af: I want to be Afghan with my Afghan friends, and Norwegian with my Norwegian friends and colleagues.
sentences.Jeg har ikke mistet kulturen min, men je: I haven't lost my culture, but I have picked up lots of Norwegian habits.
sentences.Blant annet har jeg brødskiver med bruno: Among other things, I have slices of bread with brown cheese in my packed lunch, and I try not to stand out too much from the group.
sentences.Hva er det viktigste man kan gjøre for å: What is the most important thing you can do to become integrated and get a job in Norway?
sentences.Det viktigste du kan gjøre, er å lære sp: The most important thing you can do is to learn the language and understand Norwegian society.
sentences.Det er ikke lett, men jeg mener at det e: It isn't easy, but I believe it is necessary in order to find a job and live well in this society.
That's why you have to work hard.
sentences.Hva kan lærerne og de som jobber med fly: What can teachers and those who work with refugees do?
sentences.Det er viktig at lærere ser og lytter ti: It is important that teachers see and listen to their pupils.
sentences.De må starte på nytt med nesten alt, og: They have to start again with almost everything, and they are far away from family and friends.
sentences.Det er ofte en grunn til at en elev er u: There is often a reason why a pupil can't concentrate.
sentences.Jeg husker spesielt én lærer veldig godt: I remember one teacher especially well.
sentences.Hvis hun så at jeg var ukonsentrert i ti: If she saw that I couldn't concentrate in class, she talked to me after class, maybe just for two minutes.
She asked me if everything was all right.
sentences.Jeg svarte ikke alltid på spørsmålene he: I didn't always answer her questions, but I liked that she asked.
sentences.Hva liker du best med Norge?: What do you like best about Norway?
There is a lot that I like about Norway.
sentences.Jeg liker naturen og de norske verdiene,: I like the nature and the Norwegian values, for example that there is democracy and freedom of speech here.
sentences.Det aller beste er likestillingen mellom: The very best thing is the equality between men and women, and that a human being is seen as a human being.
sentences.Når barna blir litt større, vil Abdul st: When the children are a bit older, Abdul wants to study more.
sentences.Han vil jobbe hardt, og han har lyst til: He is willing to work hard, and he would like to become a social worker.
sentences.Enslige mindreårige flyktninger er under: Unaccompanied minor refugees are under 18 and come to the country without parents or others with parental responsibility.
sentences.Mange bor i en bolig sammen med andre en: Many live in a home together with other unaccompanied minors, and some live in a foster home.
sentences.Å bo i fosterhjem er å bo hos en vanlig: Living in a foster home means living with an ordinary family.
sentences.Røde Kors Ungdom finnes i hele landet og: The Red Cross Youth exists all over the country and runs activities for young people between 13 and 30.
sentences.De vil skape et bedre liv for unge menne: They want to create a better life for young people through voluntary work.
sentences.De arbeider for økt forståelse, medmenne: They work for greater understanding, compassion and tolerance.
sentences.De organiserer aktiviteter på asylmottak: They organise activities at asylum reception centres and other meeting places.
sentences.De arbeider også for å knytte kontakt me: They also work to make contact between young refugees and people from the local community.
